claims.rationale: Of the five do-now tasks measured 2026-08-19 (T378/T455/T448/T454/T442), three serve L1 (T455, T448, T454), two serve L4 (T378, T442), and zero serve L2. The brief's pre-measured finding survives: the do-now queue advances L1 and L4 only, with no L2 representation; T467 (in progress) is a ruling on L2, not evidence production. Confirms the operator's worry that infrastructure is displacing the mission, while honestly noting the sequencing rationale (instruments before claims).

L6 (small Go solved, certifiably) is the convergence point of L2+L4+L5; no individual task can advance L6 on its own. The kanban has zero rows whose primary chain is L6. This is by design, not a gap — but it is the most surprising reading of the distribution and is worth surfacing.

T458 (disambiguate 'row') is genuinely necessary work and has no landmark on the map. Propose L8 (the language the project speaks is unambiguous): a human can see at a glance whether 'row' means a kanban task or a register claim, because every agent reads the disambiguated file first.

T328 (bake-off harness) is genuinely necessary work and has no landmark on the map. Propose L9 (the fleet can race its own workers on demand): a human can run `tools/bakeoff.sh <prompt>` and see the per-model answer, ranked. Races themselves are evidence for L1/L2/L4, but the *ability to race* is its own capability.

T349 is a malformed registration (shell-quoting accident), superseded by T352; the row carries no work and was failed on purpose. Its only honest role is to record that the registration was wrong; questioned in landmark assignment because there is nothing it would do.

The phantom stub '--bundle' references untracked/T430-phase2-audit.md, verified absent on disk 2026-08-19; only T433-phase2-audit.md exists. The phase-2 content has been delivered under T433; claim_count=0. Nothing the row would do would change the ledger; T444/T446 already recommended close-with-evidence.
